# Recipe — add a boot node

## 0. First, prove it should be a boot node

**A thing becomes a boot node if and only if it must be _awaited_, OR can _fail meaningfully_, OR
needs _external ordering_.** If none of the three hold, stop — it is not a boot node.

| Answer | Tier | What you write instead |
|---|---|---|
| None of the three | **1** — plain DI construction | A constructor. The container builds it; no node. |
| It is **feature** startup (a mission, a shop refresh, a match setup) | **3** — `IAsyncStartable` in the feature's own child scope | Startup owned by the scene/gameplay scope. |
| At least one of the three, and it is **framework/app-wide** | **2** — `IBootNode` | Continue below. |

**A `MissionInit` node placed in the kernel is a boundary violation.** The kernel is
feature-agnostic by design — it must not know your game features exist. That is why this law is
enforced by review and not by the kernel.

**Adding a boot node to the kernel is a spine change** (`AGENTS.framework.md` §6) — route it. A
tier-3 feature startup in your own scope is not, and needs no routing.

## 0a. Where the files go

A boot node is an **adapter** — it awaits work, it can fail, it touches the outside world — so it
lands in `Assets/<Sku>/Features/<Feature>/Infrastructure/` (`namespace Game.Infrastructure`), with a
`Game.Infrastructure.asmref` in that folder. Its **capability declarations** are engine-free data and
belong one tier down, in `.../Application/` (`namespace Game.Application`) — that is what lets another
tier name a cap without dragging an adapter along. The registration that hands the node to the kernel
is a `.../Composition/` concern.

The emitted boot starter is exactly this shape: `Features/Boot/Application/GameBootCaps.cs` plus
`Features/Boot/Infrastructure/{LoadingSceneHost,LoadingSceneNode,TestWaitNode,GatedFirstSceneNode}.cs`.

## 1. Declare capabilities, never node names

The kernel reasons **capability → capability**. It never knows one node's name from another.

```csharp
public string Id => "ShopCatalog";
public IReadOnlyList<BootCap> Requires => new[] { BootCaps.ConfigAvailable, BootCaps.UserDataLoaded };
public IReadOnlyList<BootCap> Provides => new[] { GameBootCaps.ShopCatalogReady };
```

Framework capabilities available: `LoggingReady` · `ConfigAvailable` · `UserDataLoaded` ·
`LocalizationReady` · `AssetReady` · `UiReady` · `ConsentResolved` · `ClockSynced` ·
`RemoteConfigFresh` · `AdsReady` · `IapReady` · `AnalyticsReady`.

A SKU declares its own caps in its `GameBootCaps` (the Setup Wizard emits a starter).

## 2. The race rule — the whole point of the graph

> **A node ctor-injects only services whose readiness is asserted by its `Requires` caps.**

Injecting a service whose readiness your `Requires` does not assert **is** the race the boot graph
exists to prevent (rule #5). If you need `IGameConfig`, you must require `ConfigAvailable`. No
exceptions, and no "it happens to work in practice".

## 3. Fill in the rest of the surface

| Member | Choose |
|---|---|
| `Required` | `true` ⇒ failure aborts boot (`BootAbortedException`) + error screen. `false` ⇒ logged to the report, boot continues. Default to `false` unless the game is genuinely unplayable without it. |
| `SoftTimeout` | Elapsed ⇒ `Degraded`, **and the background task keeps running** — a late arrival is still usable. |
| `HardTimeout` | Elapsed ⇒ the task is actually cancelled. |
| `Predicate` | `false` ⇒ `Skipped`, and it **still emits `Provides`** — so dependents are not stranded. |
| `ExclusiveGroup` | Same non-empty group ⇒ the scheduler serializes those nodes. Use for a shared exclusive resource. |
| `Weight` | Relative cost, **never a duration**. Only the `Framework/Boot Graph` preview reads it. |

## 4. Do your own threading

**The framework never moves your node off-thread** (rule #6). CPU-heavy work self-hops inside
`RunAsync`:

```csharp
await UniTask.RunOnThreadPool(() => ParseTheBigCatalog(), cancellationToken: ct);
```

## 5. Gate

```
Framework/Boot Graph          # preview the scheduled order before running anything
```

`BootGraph.Validate()` rejects a missing or cyclic capability before boot starts, and runs in the
headless `TestCategory=DataValidation` subset. `Framework/Doctor` check 7 runs it too.

Note that the **real** SKU node list is DI-assembled, so the authoritative gate is the Unity
`-runTests` step plus an actual runtime boot; the pre-compile gate validates the graph *logic*.
A new boot node is **bootstrap/wiring**, so it earns the one **boot smoke** §8a allows — take it once
when the node is done (`pf-gates` has the procedure); the PlayMode *suite* stays CI's.

## Common failures

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| A service is null / half-built inside `RunAsync` | The race rule was broken — you injected something your `Requires` does not assert. |
| Boot hangs | A node awaits forever with no `HardTimeout`. |
| Boot aborts on a non-essential failure | `Required` is `true` where it should be `false`. |
| A dependent never runs when a node is skipped | Nothing — `Skipped` still emits `Provides`. If a dependent is stranded, the cap is missing from `Provides`. |
| Nothing renders while booting | Expected. The boot cover is **SKU-owned**; the framework renders no boot progress. |
